convoLines.text: "Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. My wound needs a second pair of hands. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"Every day it's angrier. I need it cleaned before it turns — I can't work a wound like this. Wrap it tight when you're done."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"We lost Felicia and Vikram. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"My cut needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Felicia is gone and Vikram is gone. The fire doesn't care. That's what gets me — the fire doesn't care."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"I wake before anyone else. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Nobody says Vikram's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Alright. Catch you later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Maypop — I keep thinking about what you said. I'm seeing it everywhere now."
There's an ease between you now — the kind that takes weeks to build.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that plant lesson."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Everyone gets forgotten eventually. I'm negotiating for later rather than sooner.
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
It's quiet at the ridge. Dilnaz doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Someday kids will sit by a fire and hear what I did. I want it to be a good one."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on wanting to be remembered."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Dilnaz grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Dilnaz is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "I know you and Felicia were close. I'm sorry."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hey — I found some Maypop today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Halfway to the tree line, Dilnaz freezes. Fresh tracks — big. "We go back now. Quietly." You do. The wild, reminding you.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that plant lesson."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"Right. Go on, then."

"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 12 days back. Still on your mind? 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.' We still owe that wound care a proper ending, too."
"I eat fast and leave early. Not hiding. Just — scheduling."
"It'll break at a moot or it'll break at midnight. I'm betting moot."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."

"This was good." They mean it.
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet."

Hassan shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"Fine." Sharp. "You want to hear it? I dug it up. I was starving and your hole was right there. Happy now?"
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"Caleb is gone, Priya is gone, Petra is gone, Meera is gone, and Sari is gone. The fire doesn't care. That's what gets me — the fire doesn't care."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I asked Caleb about what you believe in — Caleb's gone. Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything. Extremely normal, all of it."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it."
They pull back half a step — not leaving, just... further.
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Well. Still on what you believe in."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Thank you. Really."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Dilnaz nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.

"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Omaha, Nebraska. You looked at me like I mattered, and I wanted to keep that. So I gave you someone worth looking at. That person isn't real. This one is — and it's worse, isn't it?"
Your silence lands wrong. They look away.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They nod, already turning away.

lines: d40: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Felicia Webb is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d40: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d40: 🕯️ Felicia is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d40: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer.
d40: 🕯️ Felicia Webb is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d40: What Felicia kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d40: "Felicia's gone." Catalina looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Felicia." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d40: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Emma blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d40: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 1). Ground them: 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch. Breathe with them. Slow is fast.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Managing Fear (Level 1). Fear is data, not orders. Acknowledge it, then decide anyway. Courage is fear that kept going.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
d40: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d40: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Felicia Webb, 40 days. The mantle passes to Emma Keller.
d40: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Emma Keller, 62 — an army medic. Her hands know different work now: The Touch, Purify, Berserker Rage, Battlefield Grace, Dowsing, Translator.
d40: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Healer of the Shepherd of the Dead." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d40: The village's quarrel was with Felicia — and Felicia is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d40: You knew Felicia — not the office, the person. The fire keeps expecting them, and so do you. That's a heavier kind of stepping up. (+5 trauma)
d40: At the grave, Pablo, Vikram, Dilnaz and 7 more speak for Emma — "Felicia trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d40: The fire knew Emma before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.
